questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the context.**

The condition of children at the shelter homes is pathetic. It shows that their caretakers remain ____ concerning this.
questions.solution:
The first sentence refers to the condition of children at the shelter homes as ‘pathetic’, which is a word with a negative connotation. The second sentence continues and elaborates upon this point and out of all the given options, the word ‘**callous**’ which means ‘insensitive or cruel’ is best suited to refer to the ‘caretakers’.

Here are the meanings of some of the other options:

 
• **Liberal** – open-minded, respectful of individual rights
 
• **Tolerant** - willing to accept behaviour and beliefs that are different from your own

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Rani has ________ about the sanitation in the colony. She can’t stop thinking about it.
questions.solution:
The idiom **‘have a bee in your bonnet’** is used to refer to a situation in which a person feels very strongly about a subject and keeps thinking or talking about it.

Hence, **option 3** is correct.

Here are the meanings of the other idioms:

 
• **A bed of thorns **– a situation full of difficulty
 
• **A bird’s eye view** – a view from a high angle
 
• **Have a bone to pick** - to want to talk to someone about something annoying they have done

Note: (In the released official paper solutions, the answer has been incorrectly marked as **option 2**).

questions.question: Which of the following words should be filled at (3) as per context of the passage from the given option?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **poach**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• While all of the given options convey somewhat similar meanings, the word ‘poach’ is used in a specific context ie. it is used to refer to illegal hunting, especially on protected land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The Delhi Government recently laid the foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk.

options.text: The redevelopment project for the foundation stone for Chandni chowk was recently laid by the Delhi Government.
The foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk has recently been laid by the Delhi Government.
The foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk is recently being laid by the Delhi Government.
The foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk was recently laid by the Delhi Government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk was recently laid by the Delhi Government.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is '**The Delhi Government**'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is '**the foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk**'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'laid' will be changed into 'was recently laid'. 
 
• Lastly, the 'by' preposition will be added. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.

 ​

Correct Sentence:__ *The foundation stone for the redevelopment project for Chandni Chowk was recently laid by the Delhi Government.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• **Adverb of frequency (laid) **always comes between the auxiliary verb and the main verb.* *

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My grandfather ________ three years old.
questions.solution:
The context of the sentence suggests that the event (grandfather dying) took place in the past. Hence, options 1 and 3 are incorrect.

To establish this time period properly, we must make use of the construction ‘**when** I was’.

Hence, option 4 is incorrect.

**Option 2 is correct **since it fulfils these conditions and meaningfully completes the sentence.

Correct sentence:

*My grandfather **died when I was** three years old.*

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

It is felt by some people that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.

options.text: Children and teenagers feel that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at some people.
Some people it is feeling that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.
Some people it has felt that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.
Some people feel that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. **Some people feel that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.**

__Explanation__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e97c856a86e7f9a2254b6d21594beffe8b2a2afbb0c5bd00cd60b251c8f9881c.png] 

While converting a sentence to active voice:​

 
• The **subject **and **object **change their places.
 
• '**is/are + V₃'** is changed into the '**V₁**' form of the verb.
 
• The preposition 'by' is removed before the object.

Hence, the active sentence should be: *Some people feel that advertising for unhealthy snacks should not be directed at children and teenagers.*

questions.question: Rathore helped the farmers in multiple ways. In which of the following he did not intervene?

options.text: Encouraged the farmers to do integrated farming
Taught them to grow paddy using conventional methods
Offered them seeds and saplings of vegetables
Helped them to sell their yield in Patna, Ranchi and other towns.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.**

The passage talks about a number of ways in which Suhawan Singh Rathore’s interventions helped improve the lives of the farmers. But nowhere in the passage does it state that he *‘taught the farmers to grow paddy using conventional methods’.*

The points mentioned in the other options have been clearly credited to Rathore, but not option 2.

questions.question: From the reading of this passage it can be inferred that it is
questions.solution:
A ‘a newspaper feature’ is a report of a person or event that is presented in an interesting way and is published in newspapers. It is different from a news story in that it is written more informally and stylistically than a formal, information-based news piece.

Similarly, survey reports and investigation proceedings have very formal, distinct styles of writing and serve specific purposes.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question: Suhawan Singh Rathore went back to his village mainly because he wanted to

options.text: help the farmers of the village where he had grown up.
utilize his education for the development of his village.
fight with the Maoists who threatened the developmental projects.
do organic farming in his village.

questions.solution:
We need to use the information we derive from the passage to solve this question.

The point in option 3 is not mentioned anywhere in the passage and is hence, incorrect.

As for the other three options, while they all convey accurate information in a way, the only option that best captures the overall purpose of Rathore’s decision to go back to his village is **option 2.**

questions.question: What does ‘integrated farming’ imply?
questions.solution:
From the context of the passage, we can understand what is meant by ‘integrated farming’, particularly from the given part:

*“I did not intend to wean the farmers from conventional farming but wanted them to take to integrated farming soon after the paddy is harvested. We are offering them seeds and saplings for vegetable cultivation on the side. We have brinjal, tomato, turnip, broccoli, radish and carrot. The idea is if one crop fails, the farmer can compensate with other crops,”*

We can see that the definition of ‘integrated farming’ based on this passage is **option 4** ie. simultaneous farming of multiple crops.

questions.question: What is the future plan of Suhawan and the farmers?

options.text: to sell the products themselves in towns
to grow vegetables along with the paddy
to start their processing units and shops and employ youths

questions.solution:
Let us look at this part of the passage:

*““We will soon have **processing units and shops** where we can **engage several unemployed youths**,” he (Rathore) says.”*

Hence, we can see that the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Given below are six sentences, four of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.**

Sentence 1. At least 370 residents of the islands of Java and Sumatra were killed on Saturday when a sudden tsunami struck the coastline.

P. While Indonesia has tsunami-detection buoys positioned off its coastlines, they have not functioned for six years.

Q. An eruption of the volcano Anak Krakatau set off an underwater landslide at 2130 hours local time Saturday, triggering a giant tsunami.

R. But given the landslide’s proximity to inhabited areas, an early-warning system may not have affected the outcome, according to experts.

S. Anak Krakatau, is located at the entrance to the Sunda Strait, about 20 nm from the nearest populated shores.

Sentence 6. In addition to the rising death toll, more than 1450 were injured in the disaster, and another 130 remain missing.
questions.solution:
The first sentence introduces the main topic of the tsunami, and its consequences.

**The sentence that most logically follows sentence 1 should be Q**, since it expands on the topic of the tsunami by describing why and how it was triggered.

**The next sentence should be S** since it expands upon the topic of Anak Krakatau, mentioned previously in sentence Q.

Out of the two remaining sentences, the sentence that comes first must be P since sentence R directly references and expands upon the tsunami-detection system first introduced only in P.

Hence, the correct order should be: **QSPR**.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The invigilator told the candidates not to keep any papers with them in the examination hall.

options.text: The invigilator said to the candidates, “Don’t keep any papers with you in the examination hall.”
The invigilator asked the candidates, “Have you kept any papers with you in the examination hall.”
The invigilator said to the candidates, “Let’s not keep any papers with us in the examination hall.”
The invigilator told the candidates, “Not to keep any papers with them in the examination hall.”

questions.solution:
In the given sentence, the invigilator is addressing the students directly and telling, not asking them about something.

**Hence, options 2 and 4 are incorrect.**

Since this is a clear instruction for the students, it is unlikely that the invigilator would use the pronoun ‘us’. **Hence, option 3 is incorrect.**

**Hence, the correct answer is option 1**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

In Spain, grapes are many in demand in winters.
questions.solution:
The phrase **‘much in demand’** is used to mean that something is popular and that a lot of people want it.

The correct sentence should be: *In Spain, grapes are **much** in demand in winters.*

The words ‘many in demand’ do not form a meaningful phrase and do not convey the intended meaning.

Hence, the error in the sentence is mentioned in **option 1. **

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Suresh said to Dinesh, “Yesterday I saw a very good film at Chanakya.”

options.text: Suresh said to Dinesh that yesterday I saw a very good film at Chanakya.
Suresh told Dinesh that he had seen a very good film at Chanakya the day before.
Suresh told Dinesh that yesterday he saw a very good film at Chanakya.
Suresh asked Dinesh if he had seen a very good film at Chanakya the day before.

questions.solution:
Here are the rules we need to convert the sentence from direct to indirect:

 
• Change the verb inside the quotation marks from past tense to past perfect tense.
 
• Use pronouns appropriately: ‘I’ turns to ‘he’.
 
• The sentence is a statement, not a question. Hence, option 4 is incorrect.

The only sentence that follows these rules is **sentence 2.**

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Given below are six sentences, four of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.**

Sentence 1. Bill held open the door and I looked around.

P. I prayed to be away from this place.

Q. There were a dozen or so beds in small, partitioned cubicles along the walls of a large room.

R. The wheezing sound of respirators filled the air.

S. Most of the beds were occupied by patients who were wired to all kinds of machinery.

Sentence 6. Instead, I was wheeled over to a bed with a number printed behind it on the wall – No. 10
questions.solution:
• Out of all the given options, **sentence Q most logically follows sentence 1** since it describes the scene that immediately follows the opening of the door in sentence 1.
 
• The **next sentence should be S** since it directly follows the topic of ‘beds’ introduced in sentence Q.
 
• Similarly, the **next sentence should be R** since it talks about ‘respirators’ referring to the ‘machinery’ mentioned in sentence S.
 
• The n**ext sentence will obviously be P**.

Hence, the correct order of sentences will be **QSRP**.

Therefore, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I don’t know where _________.
questions.solution:
In the given question, we can see that the word ‘where’ is being used to join two clauses. It functions here as a subordinating conjunction to show a relationship between two clauses involving a transition of place.

The first clause here is ‘*I don’t know’*. Similarly, the second clause should follow a standard grammatical structure of **a subject followed by a predicate.**

Only **option 3** contains such a clause and is hence, the correct answer.

The correct sentence should be:

*I don’t know where the children have gone.*
